(28)
199.] If a single groove of this form be made in a conductor
having the rest of its surface plane, and if the other conductor is
a plane surface at a distance $A$, the capacity of the one conductor
with respect to the other will be diminished. The amount of
this diminution will be less than the $\frac{1}{n}$ th part of the diminution
due to $n$ such grooves side by side, for in the latter case the
average electrical force between the conductors will be less than
in the former case, so that the induction on the surface of each
groove will be diminished on account of the neighbouring
grooves.
If $L$ is the length, $B$ the breadth, and $D$ the depth of the
groove, the capacity of a portion of the opposite plane whose
area is $S$ will be
$$\frac{S-L B}{4 \pi A}+\frac{L B}{4 \pi\left(A+a^{\prime}\right)}=\frac{S}{4 \pi A}-\frac{L B}{4 \pi A} \cdot \frac{a^{\prime}}{A+a^{\prime}} .$$
(29)
If $A$ is large compared with $B$ or $a^{\prime}$, the correction becomes
by (28)
$$\frac{L}{4 \pi^{2}} \frac{B^{2}}{A^{2}} \log _{e} \frac{2}{1+e^{-\pi \frac{D}{B}}},$$
(30)
and for a slit of infinite depth, putting $D=\infty$, the correction is
$$\frac{L}{4 \pi^{2}} \frac{B^{2}}{A^{2}} \log _{e} 2 .$$
(31)
To find the surface-density on the series of parallel plates we
must find $\sigma=\frac{1}{4 \pi} \frac{d \psi}{d x^{\prime}}$ when $\phi=0$. We find
$$\sigma=\frac{1}{4 \pi b} \frac{1}{\sqrt{e^{-2 \frac{x^{\prime}}{b}}-1}}$$
(32)
The average density on the plane plate at distance $A$ from the
edges of the series of plates is $\bar{\sigma}=\frac{1}{4 \pi b}$. Hence at a distance
